chunks: And whatever is in it from Al-Abbas ibn Amir Al-Qaḍbani, I have narrated it from my father - may Allah have mercy on him - from Ali ibn Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi, from his father, from Al-Abbas ibn Amir Al-Qaṣbani. And I have narrated it from Jafar ibn Ali ibn Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi, from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Al-Abbas ibn Amir Al-Qaṣbani.

key_terms.أَبِي: My father, referring to the narrator of the hadith (often Ibn Abi Ya'la or similar in this context)
key_terms.الْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ عَامِرٍ الْقُصْبَانِيِّ: Al-Abbas ibn Amir Al-Qaḍbani, a narrator whose chain is being clarified
key_terms.جَدِّهِ: His grandfather, referring to the link in the second chain
key_terms.عَلِيِّ بْنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ الْك: Ali ibn Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi, a key link in the first chain

ai.seo_question: How is the transmission chain for Al-Abbas ibn Amir Al-Qaḍbani verified in Shia hadith literature?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq meticulously documents the dual transmission chains for Al-Abbas ibn Amir Al-Qaḍbani, a key narrator in the Kufan scholarly circle, to validate the authenticity of his reports within the *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih*. By tracing the lineage through both his father and the progeny of Imam al-Hasan, al-Saduq reinforces the reliability of this specific isnad, addressing potential scholarly scrutiny regarding the narrator's standing in early Shia hadith literature.
